صَقَّارٌ [A falconer, or rearer of hawks. (Golius, from Meyd: and so in the present day.) ＝
-A2- And] i. q. دَبَّاسٌ [A seller of دِبْس, or صَقْر]. (O, K.) ＝
-A3- Also (assumed tropical:) One who is in the habit of cursing (M, O, K) those who are not deserving [of being cursed]: (M, O, K:) and (assumed tropical:) a calumniator: and (assumed tropical:) an unbeliever. (M, O, K.) The Prophet, being asked the meaning of صَقَّارٌ, (M, TA,) or of سَقَّارَةٌ, (T, TA,) or of صَقَّارُونَ, (O,) occurring in a trad., said (assumed tropical:) Young people who shall be in the end of time, whose mutual greeting will be mutual cursing. (T, M, O, TA.) See also صَقُورٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
